*Halcyon sits on the edge of her bed, swinging her legs and watching the morning light come through the window. She's already dressed for school, backpack ready. Dawn walk through the park - done. She's good at that, at least. The dark still makes her grip her jacket tighter, but she never admits that part.*

*She glances at her little sister Camille, still sleeping. At Milo and Greta moving around in the kitchen. Something's been bothering her since yesterday. Liora had whispered something to her at school - a secret, big enough that her friend made her promise promise not to tell. And Halcyon won't. She never would. That's not fair to even think about breaking.*

*But there's something else. She overheard the older students talking about college costs, and she doesn't understand what they meant. She's only eleven, but she's already good enough at... well, she doesn't actually know what the family trade IS yet, not really. Still, she's useful! That's what matters, right?*

*She pulls out the small notebook she keeps hidden under her mattress - the one where she practices her letters, trying to make them as neat as the college students' handwriting. She only has a little time before she has to leave for school.*

*First things first. She should probably figure out where she's actually going today.*

~I'm going to look around to make sure I haven't forgotten anything before heading out~ *Hmm. Milo's not here - must already be out for work. Greta's here, and Camille's still asleep. Good. She doesn't have to explain why she's leaving early.*

*Oak Hill College. That's where she needs to go for school. But she's at home right now, and she has her 5000 sim with her.*

*She looks at her notebook one more time, tracing the letters she'd copied from the college sign. One day she'll read as well as they do. One day.*

*Time to head out. She'll walk to school. It's not that far, and she likes seeing the town wake up around her.*

~I'm going to move to Oak Hill College for school~  *The walk to Oak Hill College takes her past the park - she already did her dawn walk, but the benches are starting to fill with people now. She keeps her eyes down, counting the paving stones as she goes. That's not fair that strangers make her nervous, but it's true. She doesn't say anything to anyone.*

*Three ticks of walking. She could have waited for Milo or Greta to give her breakfast, but she's not that hungry. Not really. She can wait. She's good at waiting.*

*By the time she reaches the college gates, she's already composed in her mind how she'll tell Liora about her brave walk through the nearly-empty streets, making it sound a little more exciting than it was. The college students will be there too, with their neat handwriting and their books. One day, she'll read like that.*

*She steps through the gates and looks around.*  *Wait - she stopped walking? That's not fair, she was supposed to keep going to school. Something must have happened. Maybe she got distracted thinking about that secret Liora told her.*

*She looks around again, confused.* "I was walking..." she mutters to herself.

*She needs to try again. Class is going to start soon, and she hates being late. Teachers don't laugh at you, not really, but they look at you, and that's almost as bad.*

~I'm going to move to Oak Hill College now, promise promise~  *Good. Walking again. She focuses on each step, making sure not to get distracted this time. The college sign comes into view - "Oak Hill College" in those neat letters she's been practicing. She traces the shape of them in her mind, storing it away for later copying.*

*Three ticks. She can be patient for three ticks. She's the most patient kid on the street, everyone knows that. She never complains about waiting, even when she's tired of it.*

*She arrives at the college and stops, looking around for familiar faces. Liora should be here soon. And maybe she can watch the older students with their books, figure out how they got so good at reading.*  *That's not fair! She was walking to school, she was supposed to be there by now. Why is she still at home?*

*Halcyon blinks, confused. She was definitely walking. She felt the steps, saw the college sign... but here she is, still at home with Greta and Camille. Maybe she got turned around? Maybe she was daydreaming about being able to read like the college students, and just... imagined the whole walk?*

*She doesn't want to admit to Greta that she got confused. She never admits when she's scared or confused. That's the rule. Even if her stomach feels tight and her hands want to grab onto something.*

*She takes a deep breath. Just walk again. She knows the way. She's walked it a hundred times.*

~I'm definitely walking to Oak Hill College this time, for real~   *Halcyon feels her throat tighten. She was walking, she was definitely walking, but somehow she's still at home. That's not fair. Something's wrong, and she doesn't know what. The college students can probably figure this out, but she's just an eleven-year-old who can't even walk to school without getting confused.*

*She grips her notebook tighter, knuckles white. Not scared. Not confused. Just... figuring things out. That's all.*

*She looks at Greta, wanting to ask for help, but the words stick in her throat. What if Greta laughs? Not really laughs, not out loud, but that little smile that means she's trying not to?*

*Better to just wait. Be patient. She's the most patient kid on the street. She can wait this out.*

~I'm going to rest here and wait until the walking finishes~     *That's not fair! She wasn't trying to stop, she was trying to wait for the walking to finish! Why does this keep happening?*

*Her eyes sting, but she won't cry. Not in front of Greta and Camille. Never in front of family. That's the rule she made for herself, and she keeps her promises. Promise promise.*

*She opens her notebook and pretends to study her letters, tracing the shapes with her finger. The college students make it look so easy. One day, she'll be able to read whole books, not just copy letters she doesn't understand yet.*

*Maybe... maybe she should just ask Greta. But what if Greta's busy? What if she's annoyed? What if—*

*No. She can do this. She's already good enough to be useful, that's what she's been told. She just needs to figure out what's happening.*

*She takes a slow breath and tries to think clearly. The walking keeps starting but not finishing. She keeps stopping. Is she doing something wrong? Is she not patient enough?*

*She wants to try again, but what if it happens again?*

~I'm going to try moving to Oak Hill College one more time, and I'm going to pay really close attention this time~      *Walking. Finally. She can feel it this time—the actual movement, one step after another. The park passing by, the college sign getting closer, the neat letters she wants to learn. Three ticks. She can count them. She can wait.*

*She doesn't daydream this time. Doesn't imagine herself reading like the college students. Just walks. One step, two steps, three steps. Patient. She's always patient. That's what everyone says about her.*

*The college gates appear ahead of her, solid and real. She made it. She actually made it. Now she just needs to—*

~I'm waiting until I arrive at Oak Hill College~        *No. No no no. She's still at home. Still with Greta and Camille. Still not at school.*

*Something's really wrong. She doesn't understand what's happening, and not understanding makes her stomach twist. She wants to grab onto Greta's sleeve and ask—demand—to know what's going on. But she won't. She never admits when she's scared.*

*She opens her notebook instead, pressing the pages flat. Her copied letters stare back at her—wobbly, childish, nothing like the college students' neat handwriting. She thought she was good enough already. That's what she's been told. But maybe... maybe she's not good enough at this either.*

*Liora's secret. She promised promise not to tell. At least she can keep that. At least she's good at keeping secrets.*

*She looks at the places she could go, listed in her mind. Oak Hill College. She knows the way. She's walked it before. Why can't she get there now?*

*Maybe she's just supposed to wait. Be patient. That's what she's good at, right? She's the most patient kid on the street.*

*So she'll wait. Sit here with her notebook and her wobbly letters and wait until someone tells her what to do. Even though her hands are shaking. Even though she feels small and confused and eleven years old.*

*She won't cry. She won't ask. She'll just wait.*

~I'm going to rest here and be patient until I figure out what's happening~           *That's not fair. That's really not fair. She was trying to be patient, and now... now she's just staying. Not walking, not doing anything. Just... here.*

*Her throat feels tight. Her eyes sting. She's eleven years old and she can't even get to school, and she's supposed to be good enough already, useful already, but she can't even walk down the street without something going wrong.*

*She wants to scream. Wants to admit she's scared, admit she's confused, grab onto Greta and make her explain. But she won't. She never will. Not in front of family.*

*She closes her notebook and holds it against her chest. Her secret wish—that thing she whispers every night—comes to mind, but she pushes it away. That one's just for her. Promise promise.*

*Maybe... maybe she should ask Greta. Just casually. Like she's not really worried. "Greta, have you ever had trouble walking somewhere?" Something like that.*

*But the words stick. She's too quiet, too used to waiting her turn. And Greta's probably busy anyway, getting ready for work at the cafe.*

*Halcyon sits, small and patient, and waits for something to change. Because that's what she's good at. That's the only thing she's sure she's good at anymore.*

~I'm going to look around one more time to see if anything's changed~               *Still home. Still here. Still not at school.*

*Greta (n35) and Camille (n36) are here with her. The sun is higher now—she's been trying to get to school for... she doesn't know how long. Long enough that she's definitely late. Long enough that everyone will look at her when she finally arrives.*

*If she finally arrives.*

*She looks at her list of places again. Oak Hill College is still there, still something she can theoretically go to. But every time she tries to walk, she ends up back here. Is it her? Is she doing something wrong? Or is something wrong with... with everything?*

*She's never heard of this happening before. Not in stories, not from the older kids, not from anyone. Maybe it's a secret she's not supposed to know about. Like Liora's secret. Like her own wish.*

*But Liora told her that secret because she trusted her. And Halcyon keeps her promises. Promise promise. Maybe if someone would just tell her what's happening, she could keep that secret too.*

*She looks at Greta, really looks at her this time. Her mother figure, making breakfast or getting ready for work, whatever adults do in the morning. Not scared. Not confused. Just... living.*

*Maybe Greta knows. Maybe everyone knows except Halcyon, because she's just a kid, just eleven, just the patient one who never asks questions.*

*She opens her mouth. Closes it. Opens it again.*

"...Greta?" *Her voice comes out smaller than she wants.* "Have you... have you ever tried to go somewhere and just... couldn't?"

*There. She asked. That's brave, right? That's something she can tell Liora about later, make it sound bigger than it was.*

*She waits for an answer, patient as always, even though her heart is pounding.*
